title: Grace-based cache-slot holdback to preserve prefix-linearizability under continuous batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: under continuous batching we observe races where a GPU-resident KV slot is reclaimed while overlapping batched requests still reference the slot (prefix-scoped cache entries). This leads to either missing KV hits or incorrect reuse of memory (stale KV) when kernel demotion and slab compaction run concurrently. Existing LRU/TTL heuristics are insufficient because they don't account for batch pinning semantics nor prefix affinity.

Proposal: implement a lightweight "grace holdback" state machine for cache slots that cooperates with the continuous batch scheduler and the slab manager to guarantee prefix-linearizability semantics. Instead of immediately reclaiming a slot on LRU/TTL eviction, the slot transitions to HOLD for a configurable grace window or until all active batch pins for the prefix are released. While in HOLD the slot is excluded from immediate reassignment and is eligible for non-destructive demotion (move to CPU or compressed representation). Only after the hold period and zero active pins may the slot be fully evicted. The approach provides correctness guarantees (no in-flight refs to evicted prefixes) while allowing aggressive memory reclamation via demotion and coordinated compaction.

Key goals: preserve prefix correctness guarantees, limit worst-case GPU memory pressure, add minimal per-request overhead, and remain compatible with existing continuous-batching code paths.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic unit tests covering slot transitions: ACTIVE -> HOLD -> DEMOTED -> EVICTED with simulated batching pins.
Integration fuzz runs (fuzzbench harness) show zero prefix-linearizability violations across 1M synthetic requests with varying sequence lengths.
End-to-end latency regression <= 5% p95 on standard chat workload compared to baseline without grace holdback (when feature flag enabled).
Memory reclamation metrics show >= 90% of expected reclaimed bytes within 120s of eviction eligibility in heavy workload runs (with demotion enabled).
Rollout gated behind feature flag and canary with automated rollback on safety/latency/error thresholds.
design_notes: Slot lifecycle states: ACTIVE (normal), HOLD (grace window, pinned-count tracked), DEMOTED (migrated off GPU but logically present), EVICTED (freed).

Each prefix-kept entry maintains a lease token and an atomic pin count incremented by batch scheduler when a request enters a batch referencing the prefix and decremented on batch completion. The pin count is sharded per-CPU core to avoid contention.

Eviction path: eviction candidate chosen by LRU/TTL -> transition to HOLD with hold_ts set -> trigger optional demotion job (async) -> if pin_count == 0 and now >= hold_ts + hold_window -> proceed to EVICTED. If pin_count > 0, remain in HOLD until zero or max_hold_timeout triggers a forced demotion/evict with conservation fallback policy.

Demotion uses lightweight compression and a compact serialized KV representation that can be reconstructed on demand. Demoted slots are tracked in a demotion index; GPU slab metadata flags ensure compaction does not overwrite demoted slots until logical eviction completes.

Fencing: introduce a monotonically-increasing epoch counter per-shard. Batches capture epoch at start; eviction increases epoch when transitioning a prefix to tombstone. Batch replay checks epoch to detect potential stale-cache scenarios and will re-fetch from backing store if mismatch occurs.

Telemetry: expose metrics for hold_count, average_hold_duration, demotion_rate, forced_evict_count, pin_count_histogram, and prefix-tombstone events. Add structured tracing hooks for batch->pin->evict lifecycles.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal alpha): feature flag enabled on a single dev cluster; run synthetic stress tests and end-to-end chat replay for 48h.
Phase 2 (canary): enable on 5% of production serving pool for low-traffic tenants for 1 week; monitor correctness metrics and p95 latency.
Phase 3 (ramp): if canary stable, ramp to 25% then 100% over 2 weeks with continuous monitoring and automatic rollback on safety alerts.
Fallback: if forced-evict threshold exceeded, fallback to conservative TTL-only eviction for the impacted shard and send incident ticket.
testing_plan: Unit tests for atomic pin counters (sharded), slot state transitions, and epoch fencing logic.
Integration tests with continuous-batching harness simulating concurrent batch windows, kernel demotion, and slab compaction.
Fuzzbench scenario: random sequence of prefixes with hotspots and rare long-tail prefixes; run for >= 1M ops and validate no stale hits.
Performance benchmarks: measure p50/p95 token latency and GPU/CPU memory over time for baseline vs feature on (small/medium/large batch sizes).
Chaos tests: induce GC/demotion pauses and network slowness to ensure graceful degradation and automatic fallback paths.
